tagline: Leading U.S. homebuilder delivering quality homes and financial strength
hero_kpi_rationale: Key performance indicator in a margin-oriented, cyclical sector. Gross margin reflects the company's ability to navigate pressures on land costs and sales incentives, fundamental drivers of profitability in the residential construction industry.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue that remains after deducting direct construction costs.
kpis.description: Home sale gross margin declined from 28.9% in 2024 to 26.3% in 2025, decreasing each quarter, reflecting high sales incentives and higher land costs.
kpis.signal: Continued margin decline in 2025, impacted by incentives and land costs.

kpis.name: Home Sale Revenues
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from the sale of built homes.
kpis.description: Home sale revenues decreased by 3% in 2025, to $16.7 billion, due to a 5% decline in unit sales, partially offset by a 2% increase in average selling price.
kpis.signal: Revenue decline driven by fewer homes sold.

kpis.name: Net New Orders
kpis.explanation: Number of new home orders after cancellations.
kpis.description: Net new orders declined by 4% in 2025, to 27,914 units, reflecting weakened demand, particularly in Texas and the West.

kpis.name: Backlog
kpis.explanation: Value of homes ordered but not yet delivered.
kpis.description: Backlog value dropped 19% in 2025, to $5.27 billion, due to low inflow of new orders.
kpis.signal: Significant backlog decline, indicating future slowdown.

kpis.name: SG&A
kpis.explanation: Costs related to sales, administration, and management.
kpis.description: SG&A expenses increased by 19% in 2025, to $1.57 billion, largely due to changes in insurance reserves ($42.3M in 2025 vs $333.9M in 2024) and technology costs to support production volumes.

kpis.name: Closings
kpis.explanation: Number of completed and sold homes.
kpis.description: Closings decreased by 5% in 2025, to 29,572 units, due to low order intake and a weakened backlog.
kpis.signal: Lower production in response to weak demand.

kpis.name: Share Repurchases
kpis.explanation: Amount spent to buy back the company's own shares.
kpis.description: The share repurchase program reached $1.2 billion in 2025, with an additional $1.5 billion authorization approved in January 2025, demonstrating a strong commitment to shareholder value creation.
kpis.signal: Commitment to shareholder returns despite challenging market conditions.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale. Indicateur clé pour les investisseurs orientés revenus.
kpis.description: 5-year history of declared dividends per share (2021-2025).

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel du cash redistribué aux actionnaires : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury stock).
kpis.description: For 2025: cumulative dividends + share buybacks in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée en dividendes. Au-dessus de 80 % indique un dividende potentiellement non-soutenable.
kpis.description: Dividends / net income for 2025 (based on net income attributable to shareholders).

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL data across the last 8 fiscal years reported (10-K).
kpis.signal: Total Revenue of $3.192 Bn in the last fiscal year (FY2020).

risks.title: Deterioration in real estate demand
risks.score_rationale: The risk is highlighted in the context of significant volatility in new housing demand, with strong language (significant volatility, uncertainties). It is central to the building sector and directly impacts sales and margins. The Macro category is heavily weighted.

risks.title: Significant goodwill impairment
risks.score_rationale: A goodwill impairment of 28.6M in 2025 is flagged in Note 1, with clear language on non-recoverability. This reflects deterioration in the value of acquired assets. The amount is material relative to market cap and signals a decline in financial health.

risks.title: Intangible asset impairments
risks.score_rationale: Impairments of 10.8M on intangible assets are noted in 2025, linked to reassessment of their recoverability. The language is technical but the impact is concrete. This suggests loss of value in acquired brands or know-how.

risks.title: Tangible asset impairments
risks.score_rationale: A loss of 49.6M on fixed assets is recorded in Other income (expense), net, related to disposal of production assets. The amount is significant and indicates costly restructuring or divestment.

risks.title: Volatility in land acquisition costs
risks.score_rationale: Land-related charges increased to 126.9M in 2025 from 34.6M in 2024. The text mentions uncertainties in estimation. This shows pressure on land margins.

risks.title: Risks related to unconsolidated entities
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions recoverability assessment of investments in joint ventures, with possible losses if value is temporary. Investment balance is 167M in 2025, and language is cautious.

risks.title: Dependence on accounting estimates
risks.score_rationale: The Use of estimates paragraph emphasizes results could differ due to uncertainties, notably on land costs and impairment losses. The risk is recurring but not new.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in the provided documents. The company does not appear to position AI as a strategic or operational lever.
evidence: No reference to AI, algorithms, or automation in MD&A, risk, or results sections.
Discussions focus on sales incentives, land costs, and backlog management.
No mention of advanced digitalization or AI-based decision support tools.
